_comment: MCP-transport adapter — the voice loop itself becomes an MCP server (transport.type='mcp'), launched by a channel-aware host such as Claude Code via .mcp.json (see .mcp.json.example at the repo root). Spoken turns arrive at the host as a channel event; the host replies by calling the `speak` tool, which voices the text back. Copy this file, set the three discord IDs, and point stt/tts at a python that has faster-whisper + piper-tts. A leading ~ is expanded only in discord.tokenFile — use absolute paths everywhere else (never ${HOME}). For lower latency, switch stt/tts to src/stt_client.py / src/tts_client.py and run scripts/warm-servers.sh — see the README.
_transportNote: type='mcp' makes this process an MCP server. deliver='channel' (the only mode implemented in v1) pushes speech as a notifications/claude/channel event for Claude Code / channel-aware hosts. The deliver switch is the seam for future generic-host inbound modes (see docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).
